title: Which multiple of nine is closest to six thousand?
description: The remainder of six thousand on division by nine is found from its digit sum. It shows the multiple of nine just below six thousand and the one just above, and the video compares how far each is.
teaching_notes: One idea: the remainder on division by nine tells how far a number is above the multiple of nine below it, so the next multiple is nine more. Watch for students who take only the multiple below and forget to compare it with the one above.

source: Figure it Out (multiples of nine, question 3)
video_script.why: The student can find a remainder on division by nine from the digit sum and now uses the remainder to find the nearest multiples of nine.
video_script.substitution: Find the remainder from the digit sum, take it away to get the multiple below, add nine to get the multiple above, and compare the distances.
video_script.anchor: a number strip with multiples of nine marked and the number six thousand between two of them
video_script.payoff_line: The closest multiple of nine is six thousand three
maths_rules: 6000 has digit sum 6, so it leaves remainder 6 on division by 9
6000 - 6 = 5994 is the multiple of 9 just below 6000; check 5994 = 9 x 666
5994 + 9 = 6003 is the multiple of 9 just above 6000
6003 is 3 away and 5994 is 6 away, and 3 < 6
video_script.design: A number strip marks the multiples of nine. Six thousand sits six above one multiple and three below the next, so the nearer one is easy to see.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a number strip with 6000 marked and the words closest multiple of 9?

marks.ask: the number strip appears with six thousand marked and the words closest multiple of nine

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the multiple of nine that is closest to six thousand.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number sits some dots above a multiple of 9; the remainder is the gap

marks.same: the words the same way as the example in your book appear
marks.rem: the digit sum is shown giving the remainder
marks.gap: the remainder is shown as the gap between a multiple of nine and the number

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>There, we found a remainder from the digit sum.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The remainder tells us how far a number is above a multiple of nine.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number six thousand.

beats.on_screen: To find: the multiple of 9 closest to 6000

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the multiple of nine closest to it.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 6000: digit sum 6 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 6, so the remainder is 6

marks.sum: the remainder of six thousand on division by nine is asked for
marks.dsum: the digits of six thousand are added to six
marks.rem: six is marked as the remainder

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, find the remainder of six thousand on division by nine.
<bookmark mark='dsum'/>Its digit sum is six plus zero plus zero plus zero, which is six.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>Six is less than nine, so the remainder is six.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 6000 is 6 more than a multiple of 9; 6000 - 6 = 5994

marks.below: six thousand is shown six above a multiple of nine on the strip
marks.sub: six is taken away from six thousand to give five thousand nine hundred ninety four
marks.mult: five thousand nine hundred ninety four is marked as the multiple of nine below

narration: <bookmark mark='below'/>Step two, six thousand is six more than a multiple of nine.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Take six away, and six thousand minus six is five thousand nine hundred ninety four.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>That is the multiple of nine below six thousand.

marks.next: nine is added to five thousand nine hundred ninety four on the strip
marks.is: the next multiple of nine is marked as six thousand three, just above six thousand

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step three, the next multiple of nine is five thousand nine hundred ninety four plus nine.
<bookmark mark='is'/>That is six thousand three, only three more than six thousand.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 6003 is 3 away and 5994 is 6 away; 3 is less than 6

marks.away: the gap from six thousand to six thousand three is marked as three
marks.six: the gap from five thousand nine hundred ninety four to six thousand is marked as six

narration: <bookmark mark='away'/>Step four, six thousand three is three away from six thousand.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Five thousand nine hundred ninety four is six away.
<bookmark mark='close'/>Three is less than six, so six thousand three is closer.

marks.check: the digits of six thousand three are added to nine
marks.times: six thousand three is split into six hundred sixty seven groups of nine

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check six thousand three. Its digits add to nine.
<bookmark mark='times'/>It is nine times six hundred sixty seven.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The closest multiple of nine is six thousand three.
